rationale: Recording the follow-up receipt: the leadership-loss half of the read-index behaviour is now measured, so the account no longer rests partly on source reading. I write the child-level account for that question and revise the parent read-index account to fold the new receipt in, drop the limitation that said the loss path was unexercised, and add a joint history explaining how the two receipts relate.

knowledge.statement: A read request queued by a leader that has no commit in its own term is not answered while that node loses leadership: after its own quorum check demoted it to follower at its old term, no read state had appeared for the request it still owed, and nothing answered it while it was not leader. When the same node led again at a higher term and committed an entry there, the stale request was released with the read index committed at that release time (12, where the index recorded at acceptance was 10) and with the request context it was accepted with.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 52 and 54 of CheckRun 478561f525b3471ca92b9aa20c6d12df; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, ReadOnlySafe, voters {1,2,3} from equal snapshots at index=10/term=1 with node 2 never contacted; the demotion came from the node's own CheckQuorum check, and the harness writes Ready entries to storage before Advance.

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered with all four comparisons holding. While the node owed the request but was not leader, no read state was produced for it (index 52) and the demotion happened at the term the node had led at (same index), so it was the module's own quorum check rather than a peer's higher term that ended the leadership; the request therefore waited through the demotion unanswered. Once the same node led again at term 3 and committed at index 12, the stale request was released with read index 12 and with the context it was accepted with (index 54, both comparisons), so the late answer is attributable to that request and is not stale - it reports an index at least as new as the one recorded when the request was accepted. Nothing here is a defect: the module neither answers a request it cannot justify nor answers one with an outdated index, and the only gap is the one the interface documentation already permits, namely a request that is never answered at all if the node that owes it never leads again.
counterevidence: A read state appearing for the request while the node was a follower would have refuted the source reading; none appeared.
limitations: Two voters were contacted at most, so quorum was exactly the leader plus one follower; the same path with a different quorum size is not measured.
The case where the node never leads again is unobservable beyond the source fact that no other code path can answer the request.

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered, and the answered half is now measured rather than only read. With the leader elected but nothing committed in its term, the ReadIndex request produces no read state at all (index 48), which is the queueing behaviour the sources predicted; the follower's acknowledgement of that term's entry then moves the leader's commit index to 11 with a quorum of matches (index 49); and the released read state carries read index 11 together with the exact request context that was issued (index 50 for both the index and the identity comparison), so the answer is attributable to that request and is at least as new as the moment it was accepted. The remaining half of the question - a request queued by a leader that then loses leadership before committing - is now measured too: after the leader's own quorum check demoted it (StateFollower at term 2, its term unchanged, and no read state for the request it still owed, index 52), the node led again at term 3, committed at index 12, and the stale request was released there with read index 12 and the original context (index 54, both comparisons), so the late answer is attributable and not stale. The source reading's expectations were: nothing clears the queue on a term change and the release helper is reachable only from a leader path, so such a request is answered only if the same node leads again and commits, and otherwise is never answered, which the interface documentation permits by telling callers that read requests can be lost and retries are their job. Nothing here is a defect, and the finding that matters for the main account is unchanged. What used to rest on reading alone is now bounded by a receipt: nothing clears the queue on a term change, so a request owed by a demoted leader waits through the demotion, is not answered while that node is not leader, and is answered only if the same node leads again and commits - with the index reached at that later release.
counterevidence: The unanswered case is permitted by the same snapshot's ReadIndex documentation, so it cannot be scored as a defect without importing a stronger requirement than the module states.
The answered case is safe rather than merely successful: the released index is the commit index at release time, which is at least as new as the index recorded when the request was accepted.
limitations: Both halves are now measured: the completing path in one receipt and the leadership-loss path in another; what remains unmeasured is the case where the same node never leads again, which is unobservable by construction beyond the observation that no other code path can answer it, and the retry behaviour of applications.

Harness correction worth carrying forward: two earlier probes of this run left the leader unable to read its own entries back because the delivery helper never wrote Ready entries to storage, so their commit values stayed at the earlier snapshot index. That deficiency was harness-side, the affected receipts never depended on those values for any comparison, and this receipt uses the corrected helper.
Single process with hand-delivered messages and one configuration; no wall-clock or multi-host behaviour is measured.
interpretations.joint_history: Two receipts answer this question and are separate executions of two fixed experiments in the same package with the same construction (equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1, voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, real elections, in-process delivery, and a helper that writes Ready entries to storage before Advance): CheckRun d7a20d42d5b84569a0c6e4924cd577a9 measures queueing and release on a commit in the same term, and CheckRun 478561f525b3471ca92b9aa20c6d12df measures what happens across a leadership loss and a later term. Their indices come from their own streams and are not joined; together they cover both halves of the same behaviour.
